conditions.problem: Both solve unweighted minimum dominating set and output an integral vertex set.

conditions.approximation: The exact coefficient 7 is strictly smaller than 11 + ε for every ε > 0.
conditions.rounds: The newer round complexity is a universal constant, independent of ε. The older bound is f(ε), with its accuracy dependence retained. At the advertised asymptotic level the universal O(1) bound has no accuracy-dependent overhead. This does not compare unknown numerical round counts or identify f(ε) with a universal constant.
conditions.model: The newer algorithm uses broadcast CONGEST and therefore also works in LOCAL; message restrictions are stronger, not an extra graph or input requirement.
conditions.benchmark: The newer integral output is bounded against fractional OPT, which is at most integral OPT; it therefore also satisfies the older integral-OPT convention.
conditions.assumptions: Use the standard unique O(log n)-bit identifier convention. Neither statement requires an embedding, a maximum-degree bound, or an externally supplied solution. This certificate does not apply to variants with a different initial-information convention.

frontierComparisons.reason: Exact factor 7 replaces the 11 + ε planar guarantee using a universal constant round complexity, while the earlier round complexity depends on ε. The source introduction traces the constant-factor improvements; Theorem C(i) gives the new guarantee.

roundCountEvidence.explanation: Rounds 1–2: exchange identifiers then neighbor lists; decide phase-one set D using adjacencies from N(v) to candidate vertices in N²(v). Round 3: broadcast D membership; each vertex knows whether it lies in N[D]. Round 4: broadcast uncovered flags; each vertex computes residual closed-neighborhood degree. Round 5: broadcast residual degrees; each uncovered vertex chooses its dominator. Round 6: notify selected neighbors; all vertices know final membership. The source initially gives only each vertex its own ID. Unbounded LOCAL messages permit the lists. Auxiliary density c and excluded-depth-one-minor t affect local computation/analysis, not communication phases.

roundCountEvidence.explanation: The supplied weak two-colouring permits the Section 4 star-forest construction in an absolute constant number of rounds. The four-round schedule below computes exactly its final star centres without communicating the final edge orientations. Every black vertex with white children becomes a centre. An original white root remains a centre exactly when at least one of its black children has no white children. A white vertex that proposed to a black vertex is a leaf. In the all-depth-two case a root chooses one child for edge reversal, but the choice does not affect the set of centres, so the dominating-set output needs no extra round. This is an implementation upper bound derived from the paper, not a printed exact runtime or a claim of round optimality. Δ occurs in the approximation guarantee, not in the communication radius. The catalogue’s f(Δ) classification can be strengthened to constant. Schedule: (1) exchange weak-colouring bits; (2) black vertices propose to white parents; (3) white vertices without black children propose to black parents; (4) black vertices report whether they acquired white children. The selected set is the final star centres.

sourceResults.proofSketch: In a component with at least three vertices, non-leaves dominate. Assign each non-optimum vertex to an adjacent optimum vertex; the resulting disjoint stars use n−OPT edges. A pseudoforest component has at most n edges, so at most OPT edges remain outside the stars. Every non-optimum non-leaf touches a remaining edge, giving at most 2 OPT such vertices, plus at most OPT optimum vertices. Singleton and two-vertex components have ratios one and two. Sum over components.

roundCountEvidence.explanation: The supplied weak two-colouring permits the Section 4 star-forest construction in an absolute constant number of rounds. The four-round schedule below computes exactly its final star centres without communicating the final edge orientations. Every black vertex with white children becomes a centre. An original white root remains a centre exactly when at least one of its black children has no white children. A white vertex that proposed to a black vertex is a leaf. In the all-depth-two case a root chooses one child for edge reversal, but the choice does not affect the set of centres, so the dominating-set output needs no extra round. This is an implementation upper bound derived from the paper, not a printed exact runtime or a claim of round optimality. Δ occurs in the approximation guarantee, not in the communication radius. The catalogue’s f(Δ) classification can be strengthened to constant. Schedule: (1) exchange weak-colouring bits; (2) black vertices propose to white parents; (3) white vertices without black children propose to black parents; (4) black vertices report whether they acquired white children. The selected set is the final star centres.

results.assumptions:
Source result (sparse-planar-eleven), evaluated on its transformed instance: Unique identifiers; no embedding is supplied.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. This example concerns the size lemma and does not itself refute Theorem 17’s approximation ratio. Connected unweighted input. Preserve source randomness, identifiers, parameter knowledge and initial-input conventions. The displayed target benchmark is integral OPT.

roundComplexityDetails.explanation: Rounds 1–2: exchange identifiers then neighbor lists; decide phase-one set D using adjacencies from N(v) to candidate vertices in N²(v). Round 3: broadcast D membership; each vertex knows whether it lies in N[D]. Round 4: broadcast uncovered flags; each vertex computes residual closed-neighborhood degree. Round 5: broadcast residual degrees; each uncovered vertex chooses its dominator. Round 6: notify selected neighbors; all vertices know final membership. The source initially gives only each vertex its own ID. Unbounded LOCAL messages permit the lists. Auxiliary density c and excluded-depth-one-minor t affect local computation/analysis, not communication phases. The atlas applies the exact instance substitutions and communication cost of the reduction: Connect a dominating set locally.

results.assumptions:
Source result (lenzen-arboricity-deterministic), evaluated on its transformed instance: Unweighted; uniform algorithm.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. This example concerns the size lemma and does not itself refute Theorem 17’s approximation ratio. Connected unweighted input. Preserve source randomness, identifiers, parameter knowledge and initial-input conventions. The displayed target benchmark is integral OPT.

results.assumptions:
Source result (alipour-fourcycle-18), evaluated on its transformed instance: Randomized LOCAL algorithm; the no-isolated-vertex setting is used here.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. This example concerns the size lemma and does not itself refute Theorem 17’s approximation ratio. Connected unweighted input. Preserve source randomness, identifiers, parameter knowledge and initial-input conventions. The displayed target benchmark is integral OPT.

roundComplexityDetails.explanation: The supplied weak two-colouring permits the Section 4 star-forest construction in an absolute constant number of rounds. The four-round schedule below computes exactly its final star centres without communicating the final edge orientations. Every black vertex with white children becomes a centre. An original white root remains a centre exactly when at least one of its black children has no white children. A white vertex that proposed to a black vertex is a leaf. In the all-depth-two case a root chooses one child for edge reversal, but the choice does not affect the set of centres, so the dominating-set output needs no extra round. This is an implementation upper bound derived from the paper, not a printed exact runtime or a claim of round optimality. Δ occurs in the approximation guarantee, not in the communication radius. The catalogue’s f(Δ) classification can be strengthened to constant. The atlas applies the exact instance substitutions and communication cost of the reduction: Connect a dominating set locally.

roundComplexityDetails.explanation: The paper gives two phases without a total round count. A conservative implementation floods identifiers and neighbor lists for six rounds, then uses one round to notify selected neighbors. The first six rounds reveal degrees through distance five, sufficient to reconstruct the first selection and uncovered vertices within distance two. Every replacement candidate covers the selecting vertex, so it lies in its closed neighborhood. This is an implementation upper bound, not a source-stated or optimal count. The atlas applies the exact instance substitutions and communication cost of the reduction: Connect a dominating set locally.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. Source result (pic-ass-sublog-refine), evaluated on its transformed instance: A c-approximate dominating set is provided as input.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. This example concerns the size lemma and does not itself refute Theorem 17’s approximation ratio. Connected unweighted input. Preserve source randomness, identifiers, parameter knowledge and initial-input conventions. The displayed target benchmark is integral OPT.

results.assumptions:
Source result (folklore-degree-mds), evaluated on its transformed instance: Unweighted graphs. No identifiers, degree knowledge, or communication are needed.

Domination on the line graph: A selected vertex of L(G) corresponds to the original edge. Feasibility and cardinality OPT agree; weighted transfer additionally requires an algorithm accepting the corresponding vertex weights. Assign each virtual edge-node to an endpoint. With unrestricted LOCAL messages, a virtual round routes through shared endpoints in at most two physical rounds; constant setup and output notification give O(T+1). The source algorithm must accept the line graph’s n′, Δ′, IDs and any supplied parameters. Obtaining global information is not free. A line graph can be much denser and need not preserve planarity: the line graph of a star is a clique. This recipe claims LOCAL only. Arbitrary different messages along virtual adjacencies can create congestion at physical edges, so an O(T) CONGEST simulation is not inferred. Exact algorithm substitutions use n′=m and Δ′=Δ_L, where Δ_L=max_{uv∈E(G)}(deg(u)+deg(v)−2). The displayed 2Δ−2 is an upper bound, not an exact substitution in a nonmonotone theorem. For simple G, m_L=sum_v binom(deg(v),2) is the exact number of edges of L(G). It is retained symbolically rather than replaced by a monotone upper bound. Apply the dominating-set algorithm to L(G); generic transfer is certified only from unrestricted general-graph LOCAL algorithms. Virtual line-graph rounds route through shared endpoints in at most two physical rounds. Retain global-input assumptions; setup and output notification are included. Here m=|E(G)| and Δ_L=max over uv∈E(G) of (deg(u)+deg(v)−2), the exact maximum degree of L(G); Δ_L≤2Δ−2. If m=0, return the empty edge set locally. For simple G, m_L=sum_v binom(deg(v),2) is the exact number of edges of L(G). It is retained symbolically rather than replaced by a monotone upper bound.

The source CONGEST algorithm is simulated in LOCAL; this reduction claims the resulting LOCAL bound only.

reductionSteps.title: Domination on the line graph
conditions: A selected vertex of L(G) corresponds to the original edge. Feasibility and cardinality OPT agree; weighted transfer additionally requires an algorithm accepting the corresponding vertex weights.

Assign each virtual edge-node to an endpoint. With unrestricted LOCAL messages, a virtual round routes through shared endpoints in at most two physical rounds; constant setup and output notification give O(T+1).
The source algorithm must accept the line graph’s n′, Δ′, IDs and any supplied parameters. Obtaining global information is not free.
A line graph can be much denser and need not preserve planarity: the line graph of a star is a clique.
This recipe claims LOCAL only. Arbitrary different messages along virtual adjacencies can create congestion at physical edges, so an O(T) CONGEST simulation is not inferred.
Exact algorithm substitutions use n′=m and Δ′=Δ_L, where Δ_L=max_{uv∈E(G)}(deg(u)+deg(v)−2). The displayed 2Δ−2 is an upper bound, not an exact substitution in a nonmonotone theorem.
For simple G, m_L=sum_v binom(deg(v),2) is the exact number of edges of L(G). It is retained symbolically rather than replaced by a monotone upper bound.
assumptions: Apply the dominating-set algorithm to L(G); generic transfer is certified only from unrestricted general-graph LOCAL algorithms.
Virtual line-graph rounds route through shared endpoints in at most two physical rounds. Retain global-input assumptions; setup and output notification are included.
Here m=|E(G)| and Δ_L=max over uv∈E(G) of (deg(u)+deg(v)−2), the exact maximum degree of L(G); Δ_L≤2Δ−2. If m=0, return the empty edge set locally.

Source result (folklore-degree-mds), evaluated on its transformed instance: Unweighted graphs. No identifiers, degree knowledge, or communication are needed.

Connect a dominating set locally: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first. Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices. For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices. The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance. Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network. This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred. Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. The atlas therefore uses the independently checked 1+2∇₁ count. This example concerns the size lemma and does not itself refute Theorem 17’s approximation ratio. Connected unweighted input. graphNetwork.description: Certified inclusions between graph families with fixed auxiliary parameters. Upper bounds restrict to subclasses. Only edges with lower=true are used for lower bounds; unspecified excluded-minor choices are not transferred backwards. Other theorem assumptions and instance domains remain in force.

nodes.label: General
nodes.description: All finite graphs; other theorem assumptions still apply.

nodes.label: Bounded arboricity
nodes.description: Equivalent boundedness families: bounded arboricity, degeneracy and maximum average degree, with parameter changes. A numerical bound is retained in the source.

nodes.label: Bounded depth-one density
nodes.description: Bounded maximum average degree and depth-one shallow-minor density.

nodes.label: Bounded expansion
nodes.description: A fixed expansion function bounds shallow-minor density at each depth.

nodes.label: Sub-logarithmic expansion
nodes.description: Expansion f(r)=o(log r); this includes every fixed-minor-free family.

nodes.label: Minor-free
nodes.description: Algorithms here quantify over every fixed excluded minor H. An inclusion may require choosing H; lower bounds are not universal in arbitrary H.

nodes.label: H-minor-free; pw(H) ≤ 2
aliases: H-minor-free with excluded minor of pathwidth at most 2
nodes.description: Graphs excluding a fixed graph H whose pathwidth is at most 2. The pathwidth condition is on the excluded minor H, not on the input graph; the input graph can have arbitrarily large pathwidth.

nodes.label: Pₜ-minor-free
nodes.description: Graphs excluding the path on t vertices as a minor, for fixed t. Every connected component has bounded diameter; disconnected inputs are handled componentwise.

nodes.label: Excluded topological minor
nodes.description: A fixed excluded clique subdivision; the bound may depend on its size.

nodes.label: Euler genus ≤ g
nodes.description: A fixed Euler-genus bound g, including nonorientable surfaces.

nodes.label: Bounded orientable genus
nodes.description: A fixed orientable-genus bound; kept distinct from Euler genus.

nodes.label: Locally embeddable
nodes.description: Bounded depth-one density and exclusion of a depth-one K3,t minor, as defined in the source.

nodes.label: Asymptotic dimension d; radius-r balls of Euler genus ≤ g
aliases: Asymptotic dimension d; r-locally Euler genus ≤ g
Asymptotic dimension d; sufficiently large-radius neighborhoods of Euler genus ≤ g
nodes.description: Graph classes of asymptotic dimension d with a fixed control function, where every induced radius-r ball has Euler genus at most g for a sufficiently large fixed radius r.

nodes.label: Asymptotic dimension d; radius-r balls of Euler genus ≤ g with at most a apices
aliases: Asymptotic dimension d; r-locally Euler genus ≤ g with at most a apices
nodes.description: Graph classes of asymptotic dimension at most d with a fixed dimensional control function, where deleting at most a vertices from each induced radius-r ball leaves Euler genus at most g, for a sufficiently large fixed radius r. This is a local condition and does not assert global minor exclusion.

nodes.label: Bounded genus with apices
nodes.description: Bounded Euler genus after deleting a bounded number of apex vertices.

nodes.label: Planar with an attached clique
nodes.description: A planar graph with a clique glued at one vertex; includes the trivial one-vertex clique.

nodes.label: Planar
nodes.description: Graphs admitting a crossing-free drawing in the plane.

nodes.label: Outerplanar
nodes.description: Planar graphs admitting an embedding with every vertex on the outer face.

nodes.label: Triangle-free planar
nodes.description: Planar graphs with no triangles.

nodes.label: Planar without 4-cycles
nodes.description: Planar graphs without cycles of length four.

nodes.label: Trees / forests
nodes.description: Acyclic graphs. Connectivity is retained where required by a theorem.

nodes.label: Paths
nodes.description: Simple paths, without a supplied orientation.

nodes.label: Oriented paths
nodes.description: Paths with a supplied orientation; retain that additional information in lower-bound statements.

nodes.label: Cycles
nodes.description: Simple cycles.

nodes.label: Long cycles
nodes.description: Cycles satisfying the theorem’s length threshold.

nodes.label: Bounded degree
nodes.description: Maximum degree is bounded by a fixed auxiliary parameter.

nodes.label: Bounded-degree trees
nodes.description: Trees with a bounded maximum degree.

nodes.label: Bipartite
nodes.description: Graphs admitting a proper two-coloring; the coloring is not automatically supplied as input.

nodes.label: Degree-3 bipartite
nodes.description: Bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most three.

nodes.label: Weakly 2-colored
nodes.description: Graphs with a supplied weak two-coloring and the source’s isolate restriction.

nodes.label: Unit-disk
nodes.description: Intersection graphs of equal-radius disks in the plane; density can be unbounded.

nodes.label: Polynomial neighborhood-independence growth
nodes.description: Polynomial growth of independent sets in neighborhoods, rather than vertex-volume growth.

nodes.label: K₂,t-minor-free
nodes.description: Graphs excluding K₂,t as a minor for a fixed integer t≥2. Since pw(K₂,t)=2, these are included in the H-minor-free family with pw(H)≤2 by taking H=K₂,t.

nodes.label: Minor-free with domination constraint
nodes.description: Excluded clique minor plus the theorem’s γ₁(G) ≤ Cγₖ(G) condition.

nodes.label: Linklessly embeddable
nodes.description: Graphs with a linkless embedding in three dimensions.

nodes.label: No K₄,₄ subdivision
nodes.description: Graphs containing no subdivision of K4,4.

nodes.label: Triangle-free; Euler genus ≤ g
nodes.description: Triangle-free graphs of Euler genus at most g.

nodes.label: High-girth bounded expansion
nodes.description: Bounded expansion together with the source’s girth ≥ 4r+2 or 4r+3 threshold.

nodes.label: High-girth k-hop expansion
nodes.description: The source’s k-hop expansion bound and girth ≥4k+3, including connectivity where stated.

nodes.label: No short odd cycles
nodes.description: No odd cycles of lengths 3,5,…,2k−1 for the stated k.

nodes.label: Powers of paths
nodes.description: r-th powers of paths for fixed r. The whole parameterized family is not planar.

nodes.label: Path powers with endpoint leaves
nodes.description: Path powers with additional leaves at one endpoint, as in the thesis construction.

nodes.label: Arboricity at most 2
nodes.description: The fixed arboricity-two family; it contains nonplanar graphs.

nodes.label: Incidence graphs
nodes.description: Variable–constraint or set–element incidence graphs; an instance-domain restriction.

nodes.label: Planar incidence graphs
nodes.description: Planar incidence graphs; the graph is also bipartite.

nodes.label: Bounded set size and frequency
nodes.description: Incidence instances with bounded set size and element frequency.

nodes.label: Bounded treewidth
nodes.description: Graphs of bounded treewidth; the parameter remains fixed.

nodes.label: Bounded pathwidth
nodes.description: Graphs of bounded pathwidth; the parameter remains fixed.

nodes.label: K₁,ₜ-minor-free
nodes.description: Graphs excluding the fixed star K1,t as a minor. Their maximum degree is at most t−1; bounded degree alone does not exclude a large star minor.

nodes.label: Regular
nodes.description: Every vertex has the same degree. A result may additionally require a positive degree; the degree need not be bounded independently of n.

nodes.label: Pseudoforests
nodes.description: Every connected component has at most one cycle. Forests are a proper subclass; each pseudoforest is outerplanar.

problemNetwork.description: Problem relations distinguish exact formulations from fractional relaxations. An arrow runs from a special problem to a more general formulation. Only certified same-graph, objective-preserving edges enable automatic upper- or lower-bound transfer; all other arrows support structural browsing only. A fractional benchmark does not make an integral output fractional. Model, input, cost, radius, capacity, and graph-class assumptions remain attached to every result.

nodes.label: Dominating set
nodes.description: Choose a minimum-cost vertex set meeting every closed neighborhood. Output is an integral set, including in results measured against fractional OPT.

nodes.label: Total dominating set
nodes.description: Every vertex, including a selected vertex, needs a selected neighbor. Isolated vertices make the unrestricted demand instance infeasible.

nodes.label: Client dominating set
nodes.description: Only a prescribed client set must be dominated. The SUPPORTED result additionally permits preprocessing of the support topology.

nodes.label: Distance-k dominating set
nodes.description: Every vertex is within graph distance k of a selected vertex. The radius is an input or fixed parameter of the particular theorem; entries retain r when that is the symbol in their bounds.

nodes.label: Connected dominating set
nodes.description: An ordinary dominating set whose selected vertices induce a connected subgraph. Connectivity changes both feasibility and OPT.

nodes.label: Connected distance-r dominating set
nodes.description: A distance-r dominating set inducing a connected subgraph of the original graph, rather than merely of its power graph.

nodes.label: k-domination (outside the solution)
nodes.description: Every vertex outside D needs at least k neighbors in D; selected vertices are exempt. This is the definition in the indexed k-tuple papers, and differs from demanding k selected vertices in every closed neighborhood.

nodes.label: Vertex cover
nodes.description: Choose vertices meeting every edge. Distance-r and connected variants have separate problem nodes.

nodes.label: Distance-r vertex cover
nodes.description: In the indexed source, each edge uv has a selected vertex within distance r of both u and v. This is not vertex cover on the power graph. Retain the source's high-girth assumption.

nodes.label: Distance-r connected vertex cover
nodes.description: The source's distance-r vertex cover with the additional requirement that the selected vertices induce a connected subgraph of the original graph.

nodes.label: Set cover
nodes.description: Choose sets covering a universe. Distributed results use the set-element incidence graph; hitting set exchanges its two sides. Incidence planarity is a requirement on that communication graph.

nodes.label: Integral local covering
nodes.description: On the physical graph G, prescribed requests r must each have a selected candidate in a locally known nonempty C(r) contained in N[r]. Costs and their bounds follow the result.

nodes.label: Covering integer program
nodes.description: A nonnegative covering formulation with integral variables. General covering integer programs and their reductions are not interchangeable with fractional covering LPs.

nodes.label: Fractional local covering
nodes.description: Minimize the cost of a nonnegative vector with sum over C(r) at least one, where each C(r) is contained in the request's physical closed neighborhood. Output is fractional.

nodes.label: Fractional covering LP
nodes.description: A positive linear program min c^T x subject to Ax >= b and x >= 0. In the generic indexed algorithm, communication takes place on the variable-constraint incidence graph.

nodes.label: Fractional dominating set
nodes.description: Nonnegative vertex weights whose sum in each closed neighborhood is at least one. A fractional vector alone does not select a dominating vertex set.

nodes.label: Fractional vertex cover
nodes.description: Minimize the cost of nonnegative vertex values satisfying x_u + x_v >= 1 for every edge uv.

nodes.label: Fractional set cover
nodes.description: Assign nonnegative values to sets so that each universe element has total incident value at least one.

nodes.label: Maximum matching
nodes.description: Choose edges sharing no endpoints, maximizing cardinality or the supplied edge weights. Fractional and capacitated variants have separate nodes.

nodes.label: Fractional matching
nodes.description: Nonnegative edge values with incident sum at most one at each vertex. The degree-constraint relaxation can have larger OPT than integral matching on nonbipartite graphs.

nodes.label: Maximum f-matching
nodes.description: Choose each edge at most once, with at most f(v) chosen incident edges per vertex. The indexed result maximizes cardinality.

nodes.label: Maximum b-matching
nodes.description: Assign nonnegative integer multiplicities to edges with incident sum bounded by b(v). The indexed result requires a supplied Lipschitz bound on b.

nodes.label: Packing integer program
nodes.description: Maximize a nonnegative objective under nonnegative packing constraints with integer or binary variables. Variable bounds and the incidence representation are part of the instance.

nodes.label: Fractional packing LP
nodes.description: A positive linear program maximizing a nonnegative linear objective under nonnegative packing constraints. A solution is fractional unless an additional integrality or rounding theorem applies.

nodes.label: Independent set
nodes.description: Choose pairwise nonadjacent vertices maximizing size or supplied weights. Here MIS denotes the maximum optimization problem, not the maximality task.

nodes.label: Vertex-disjoint H-packing
nodes.description: The current category contains vertex-disjoint copies of a fixed pattern H. An occurrence-incidence packing formulation changes the communication representation.

nodes.label: Edge dominating set
nodes.description: Choose edges so that every edge is selected or shares an endpoint with a selected edge. This is domination on the line graph, whose structural parameters may differ from the original graph.

nodes.label: Local density
nodes.description: Estimate a per-vertex density parameter. This estimation task is kept separate from covering and packing optimization problems.

edges.reason: Use all vertices as requests and C(v)=N[v] on the same graph. Setting every cost to one preserves unweighted OPT; weighted transfer retains the source cost restrictions.
Use all vertices as requests and C(v)=N(v) on the same graph. Nonempty candidate sets require an isolate-free instance; costs and input assumptions remain required.

Use prescribed clients as requests and their closed neighborhoods as candidates on the same graph. Broadcasting client membership initializes the local covering incidences in one extra round unless these flags are supplied initially. The source model and preprocessing conventions remain required. Exact lower bounds need an explicit one-round shift and are not transferred automatically.
Use all vertices as requests and C(v)=N[v]; the fractional variables, objective, graph, and feasible solutions are unchanged. Costs must satisfy the chosen algorithm's assumptions.

The universe is V and the set for candidate v is N[v]. Simulation needs separate request/candidate copies. The incidence graph need not preserve planarity or minor bounds: planar K4 produces K4,4. Structural browsing only.

Use open-neighborhood sets N(v) on the vertex universe. This preserves the set-cover objective but changes to an incidence representation, and feasible instances exclude isolates. No generic graph-class transfer is asserted.

Use universe E and one set of incident edges per vertex: frequency is two and maximum set size is maximum degree. Its incidence graph subdivides edges; simulating the processors and preserving a message model require a separate certified reduction.

Use requests as universe elements and the requests covered by each candidate as its set. The abstract objective agrees, but a distributed set-cover theorem may assume a different incidence communication graph. Structural browsing only.

The binary incidence formulation has one covering inequality per element and a binary selection variable per set. General integer-program reductions have representation and parameter costs, so this relation alone does not establish a round complexity.

An exact binary formulation is k*x_v + sum over neighbors u of x_u >= k. The coefficient on x_v exempts selected vertices. This is not ordinary unit-demand set cover; a distributed ILP algorithm needs its own parameter and representation checks.
Ordinary domination is exactly the case k=1. Indexed algorithms for fixed k>=2 cannot be specialized without checking that their theorems permit k=1; parameter matching is deliberately not automatic.
Making every vertex a client recovers ordinary domination, but this structural relation does not discard the preprocessing and online-round conventions of the indexed SUPPORTED theorem.
Radius r=1 gives ordinary domination. Results for a specified radius, or a girth threshold depending on that radius, require explicit parameter matching before a bound can be specialized.
Radius r=1 gives ordinary connected domination, with connectivity measured in the original graph. A theorem's allowed radii and graph assumptions must be checked explicitly.

Relaxing binary selection to nonnegative vertex values changes feasibility and OPT. A fractional solution requires an additional rounding theorem to become an integral dominating set; integral lower bounds need not apply to the LP.
Replace binary vertex selections by nonnegative values. The fractional optimum can differ, and no integrality or rounding factor is supplied by this edge.
Allow fractional set values in place of binary selections. This does not provide an integral set cover or transfer an integral-output lower bound.
The covering sets stay local, but dropping integrality changes the feasible solutions and benchmark. Integral algorithms measured against fractional OPT still belong to the integral-output problem.
Dropping the integer restrictions gives a positive fractional covering LP. The LP algorithm supplies fractional values, not a solution of the covering integer program.

Its candidate matrix is a positive covering LP. A generic algorithm communicates on a variable-constraint incidence graph, whereas the local algorithm communicates on the original graph. This representation change needs an explicit simulation.
Use the vertex universe and closed-neighborhood sets. Fractional OPT agrees, but the set-cover incidence graph is a different graph and may not preserve the target graph class.

The edge universe and incident-edge sets give frequency two. The variable-constraint network subdivides the original edges, so model and simulation details remain separate from this structural relation.
The binary incidence matrix is a positive covering LP. Coefficient encoding, normalization, variable-constraint ownership, and parameter bounds must match the selected theorem before applying it.
Relax edge indicators to nonnegative values satisfying the degree constraints. Odd cycles can separate fractional and integral OPT; this edge contains no rounding algorithm.

Use edge variables and one incident-sum constraint per vertex. A generic packing algorithm operates on the incidence network and must be simulated on the original graph with its coefficient and message-size assumptions.

Unit vertex capacities f(v)=1 recover cardinality matching on the same graph. The indexed f-matching theorem has its own capacity and supplied-expansion assumptions; a unit-capacity specialization is not inferred automatically.
Unit capacities b(v)=1 force edge multiplicities to be zero or one, recovering cardinality matching. Capacity and supplied Lipschitz-bound assumptions must be instantiated explicitly.

Use binary vertex variables with x_u+x_v<=1 on every edge and x_v<=1 for every vertex, including isolates. This exact integer formulation does not certify communication on its constraint incidence graph.

Exact occurrence formulation: one binary variable per candidate copy of H and a sum-at-most-one constraint per physical vertex. This follows from vertex-disjointness; occurrence enumeration and incidence-network simulation need separate analysis.
Use binary edge variables and sum of incident variables at most one at each vertex. This objective-preserving formulation alone does not certify a distributed integer-program simulation.

Use binary edge variables with each incident sum bounded by f(v). Integer capacities and the original graph representation remain essential; this structural formulation supplies no simulation theorem.
Use nonnegative integer edge variables with incident sum bounded by b(v). Multiplicities are allowed. This formulation does not remove the indexed algorithm's supplied Lipschitz-bound assumption.

Dropping integer or binary requirements leaves the positive packing LP, including any explicit variable upper bounds. Fractional feasibility and fractional OPT do not provide an integral output without additional rounding.

Edges of G become vertices of the line graph L(G), with adjacency when the original edges meet. Dominating sets correspond exactly, but graph classes, degrees, process ownership, and message-model simulations can change. Structural browsing only.

Use universe E and, for each candidate w, the set of edges uv for which both d(w,u)<=r and d(w,v)<=r. This is an exact reformulation of the source definition; its incidence network and communication distances change, so no bound transfers automatically.
A connected dominating set remains feasible for ordinary domination. On connected unweighted inputs, comparing integral optima gives factor 3 with the same round complexity.

Connect a dominating set in four extra LOCAL rounds on connected unweighted inputs with distinct identifiers. The checked multiplier is 1+2∇₁ (7 on planar graphs, 3 on pseudoforests); see the recipe for the source size-bound clarification.

Maximum |E(H)|/|V(H)| over depth-one shallow minors H of the input graph; needed only for the size analysis

conditions: The input is nonempty, connected and unweighted, and nodes have distinct identifiers. Run the source MDS algorithm on this same graph first.

Three LOCAL rounds reveal radius-three neighborhoods including dominating-set flags. Nearest-dominator clusters, with identifier tie-breaking, have radius one; contracting them produces a connected depth-one minor H with |D| vertices.

For each adjacent cluster pair choose one canonical dominator-to-dominator path of length at most three. In one more round its endpoints notify its at most two internal vertices. Return D and all selected internal vertices.

The checked size count is |D′|≤|D|+2|E(H)|≤(1+2∇₁)|D|. As OPT_f(MDS)≤OPT_MDS≤OPT_CDS, integral or fractional MDS benchmarks can seed an integral-OPT_CDS guarantee; the original benchmark stays in source provenance.

Planar shallow minors have density at most 3, giving multiplier 7. Forest and pseudoforest shallow minors have density at most 1, giving multiplier 3. These bounds also apply through the graph-class inclusion network.

This connector uses unrestricted LOCAL messages. A CONGEST or Anonymous source algorithm can seed it in LOCAL with the necessary identifiers; the derived algorithm is labelled LOCAL. No four-round CONGEST/anonymous connector or lower-bound transfer is inferred.

Clarification pending: preprint Lemma 16 states the stronger size bound 2d|D|. On P9, D={2,5,8} and valid depth-one density bound d=1 give 6, but every connected dominating set has size at least 7. upper.title: Bonamy–Cook–Groenland–Wesolek
upper.statement: Ratio 5 is achieved in universally constant anonymous rounds.

lower.title: Bonamy–Cook–Groenland–Wesolek
lower.statement: Every ratio below 5 is impossible in deterministic LOCAL with n-independent locality.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integral benchmark; fixed genus when relevant.
certificates.statement: Ratio 7 is tight, including the stated fixed-surface upper bound.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Ratio 7: universal rounds on planar graphs; genus-dependent rounds on fixed surfaces.

lower.title: Hilke–Lenzen–Suomela
lower.statement: Deterministic local planar approximation below 7 is impossible.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds · joint n and ε dependence
certificates.parameterDomain: log(n)/n < ε < 1; deterministic algorithms.
certificates.statement: The round complexity is Θ(log* n / ε).

upper.title: Faour–Kuhn
upper.statement: The upper bound holds for maximum-weight independent set on unrooted trees in CONGEST.

lower.title: Faour–Kuhn
lower.statement: The matching lower bound holds for unweighted oriented paths even in LOCAL.

certificates.parameterDomain: k ≥ 1; fixed k-hop expansion bound and girth ≥ 4k+3; connected input.
certificates.statement: The dependence k + f(k)^(k/(k+1)) is tight up to multiplicative constants.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: This approximation order is achieved in 3k rounds with small anonymous messages.

lower.title: Lenzen–Wenning
lower.statement: No deterministic n-independent algorithm improves the approximation order, even with identifiers.

certificates.scopeLabel: Minimum k rounds · factor independent of Δ
certificates.parameterDomain: k ≥ 2; fixed expansion bound at least 1; classes include trees of arbitrarily large degree.
certificates.statement: Exactly k rounds are sufficient and necessary for a factor independent of Δ; the upper coefficient is not certified optimal.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: A factor 2k f(k)+1 is achieved in exactly k rounds.

lower.title: Lenzen–Wenning
lower.statement: At k−1 rounds a factor smaller than Δ is impossible already on trees.

certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed α ≥ 2; known Δ for the upper; polylogarithmic approximation factors in Δ.
certificates.statement: The degree-dependent round order is Θ(log Δ / log log Δ), not the approximation coefficient.

upper.title: Alipour–Farokhnejad
upper.statement: A deterministic CONGEST upper bound attains this round order with O(α log Δ / log log Δ) approximation and one-bit messages.

lower.title: Dory–Ghaffari–Ilchi
lower.statement: The matching lower bound for constant or polylogarithmic approximation already holds at arboricity 2, even in LOCAL.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ρ, b, ε
certificates.parameterDomain: ρ ≥ 1; fixed positive integer b; fixed 0 < ε < 1/4; unit costs for MDS.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); parameter dependence is not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Integral local covering admits the upper bound; unit-cost MDS is a special case.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: The lower bound already holds for deterministic MDS on cycles.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer a ≥ 1; every minor has density at most a; lower path-power radius r=a.
certificates.statement: The coefficient is tight on these density classes; round dependence on a is not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: The upper coefficient is 2a+1 against fractional OPT.

lower.title: Amiri–Siebertz
lower.statement: Path powers of radius r have minor density at most r and exclude every coefficient below 2r+1.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer t ≥ 1; identifiers in {1,…,n}; use a=t in the minor-density upper bound.
certificates.statement: The endpoint-leaf lower bound is matched by the density-class upper bound.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: At a=t the upper coefficient is 2t+1.

lower.title: Picavet thesis
lower.statement: For identifiers in {1,…,n} and every function f, an f(t)-round deterministic algorithm cannot beat 2t+1 on the stated path-power family.

certificates.parameterDomain: Deterministic n-independent locality; integral benchmark.
certificates.statement: The coefficient 5 is tight; runtime constants are not certified.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: Ratio 5 is achieved against fractional OPT.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Square-grid witnesses exclude every ratio below 5, even against integral OPT.

certificates.parameterDomain: Δ ≥ 2; deterministic locality may depend on Δ but is independent of n.
certificates.statement: The degree-dependent approximation coefficient is exactly tight; runtime dependence on Δ is not certified.

upper.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
upper.statement: The theorem explicitly states a matching deterministic local upper bound.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.statement: The same coefficient is necessary on connected maximum-degree-Δ graphs, including algorithms with identifiers.

certificates.parameterDomain: Integer a ≥ 1; isolate-free inputs; fractional total-domination benchmark.
certificates.statement: Coefficient 2a is tight against fractional OPT; neither integral-benchmark tightness for a>1 nor optimal runtime is claimed.

upper.title: ASW26
upper.statement: The upper coefficient is 2a.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Treewidth-a witnesses force coefficient 2a against fractional OPT.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed nonplanar H, ε
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed nonplanar excluded minor H and fixed 0 < ε < 1/2.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); the additive inverse-accuracy term is not certified tight.

upper.title: Chang
upper.statement: A deterministic CONGEST upper bound gives this n-dependence.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: Paths and cycles require Ω(log* n) for fixed ε, already in LOCAL.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed α and ε
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed α ≥ 1 and fixed 0 < ε < 1/2.
certificates.statement: The n-dependence is Θ(log* n); joint α and ε dependence is not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Wawrzyniak
upper.statement: For fixed arboricity and accuracy, the deterministic LOCAL scheme uses O(log* n) rounds.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: The matching problem inherits the Ω(log* n) lower bound on paths and cycles.

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ε and expansion
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed 0 < ε < 1/2 and sub-logarithmic expansion bounds; unit capacities are allowed.
certificates.statement: The worst-case n-dependence is Θ(log* n); accuracy, expansion and capacity dependence are not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Witkowski
upper.statement: The f-matching scheme uses O(log* n) rounds for fixed parameters.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: Unit capacities recover ordinary matching, whose path and cycle lower bound is Ω(log* n).

certificates.scopeLabel: Rounds in n · fixed ε, L and expansion
certificates.parameterDomain: Fixed 0 < ε < 1/2, Lipschitz bound L and sub-logarithmic expansion bounds; unit capacities are allowed.
certificates.statement: The worst-case n-dependence is Θ(log* n); the other parameter dependencies are not certified.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Witkowski
upper.statement: The b-matching scheme uses O(log* n) rounds for fixed parameters.

lower.title: Chang
lower.statement: The unit-capacity case is ordinary matching and satisfies the Lipschitz promise; its path and cycle lower bound applies.

certificates.parameterDomain: Unweighted inputs; initial own-degree knowledge for the one-round construction.
certificates.statement: Ratio 3 is tight; this does not certify that all optimal-ratio algorithms need one round.

upper.title: Dory–Ghaffari–Ilchi
upper.location: Appendix A, Observation A.1; elementary extension in the atlas
upper.statement: The documented forest rule has ratio 3. The explicit atlas proof extends it to pseudoforests.

lower.title: ASW26
lower.statement: Paths rule out every coefficient below 3.

certificates.parameterDomain: Deterministic anonymous port numbering; positive integer weights; fixed degree and weight range for locality.
certificates.statement: The approximation ratio is exactly tight in this reviewed anonymous setting; runtime dependence on Δ and W is not certified.

upper.title: Åstrand–Suomela
upper.statement: The algorithm gives a weighted vertex cover of factor 2.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.statement: No deterministic local algorithm improves factor 2, even with identifiers; this includes the anonymous model.

certificates.parameterDomain: Unweighted regular graphs of positive degree; zero-round algorithm.
certificates.statement: Ratio 2 is tight over this family, using the cycle subclass as a lower-bound witness.

upper.title: Bonamy–Gavoille–Picavet–Wesolek
upper.statement: Selecting every vertex gives factor 2 without communication.

lower.title: Göös–Hirvonen–Suomela
lower.location: Section 1.4, vertex-cover approximability and cycle lower bound
lower.statement: A factor below 2 on cycles would yield a nontrivial independent set in constant time; cycles are regular.

certificates.parameterDomain: k ∈ {3,4,5,6}; outside-solution k-domination on planar graphs; deterministic n-independent locality.
certificates.statement: For these four values of k, the zero-round approximation coefficient is exactly tight.

upper.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Szymańska–Wawrzyniak–Witkowski
upper.statement: Selecting all vertices without communication gives ratio k/(k−2).

lower.title: Czygrinow–Hańćkowiak–Szymańska–Wawrzyniak–Witkowski
lower.statement: The matching lower bound allows identifiers and certifies k=3,4,5,6 only.

certificates.parameterDomain: k=r>1, r=o(log* n), fixed accuracy gap ε>0; cycles of length at least 4r+3; O(r) rounds.
certificates.statement: On this cycle specialization the coefficient 2r+1 is tight within O(r) rounds.

upper.title: Lenzen–Wenning
upper.statement: Every cycle has k-hop expansion bound 1; the k-round ratio 2k f(k)+1 specializes to 2r+1.

lower.title: Amiri–Wiederhake
lower.statement: In O(r) deterministic LOCAL rounds, ratio 2r+1−ε is impossible for the stated r and cycle lengths.
